intro:
We go through those weeks of recovery with you

A procedure is over in an hour, but recovery runs for weeks.

And through those weeks, the moments when you wonder "am I allowed to do this?" keep coming. When can I wash my face properly again? Can I have a massage? My back itches — may I scratch it?

Our care programmes exist to go through those weeks with you. Before a procedure we bring your skin condition up in advance; afterwards we help recovery pass comfortably.

Which care you can have, and from when, is advised through a medical consultation.

What sets our aesthetic care apart

The surgeon who operated also oversees your recovery care

If you have had liposuction, when and at what intensity care should begin; if you have had eyelid surgery, when facial care may start — those judgements are made by the medical team that performed the operation. Care elsewhere starts from "it should be fine"; here it starts from your chart.

We extended facial care to the body

While doing the regenerative care that calms skin after laser procedures, we kept hearing the same things: "could you look at my back too?", "the leg I had operated on still feels heavy." So we extended what we had done only for faces to the back, the legs and the whole body.

Designed by a team used to seeing skin at the level of the cell

Having a medical team that has long worked with stem cells means that, even when choosing a single treatment, they first ask whether this skin is currently recovering and whether it can tolerate stimulation.

groups.lead: We check your skin and physical condition, then select and combine the care you need. You can choose by area, from the face through to the back, legs and whole body; if you have had a procedure, we confirm which one and when before advising what care is possible.

tags.d:
There are days when you look in the mirror and think, "duller than yesterday." Days when washing more thoroughly changes nothing.

In dermatology, healthy skin is not defined as "free of disease" but as "luminous, well hydrated, firm and even in tone". Care is about creating and holding that state.

This may suit you if
  • your skin feels sensitive and dry after a laser procedure (IPL, laser toning)
  • flakes keep lifting and make-up will not sit
  • pores and sebum concern you
  • you want to bring your skin up in advance of surgery or a procedure
How it proceeds

Assessing the skin → thorough cleansing → replenishing moisture → the care you need → soothing and moisturising → sun protection. We follow the standard order of care used in dermatology.

What changes

Hydration, skin texture, settling of redness, firmness — the aim is to maintain and support your skin's condition. Skin and daily habits differ from person to person, so the same care produces different results.

When we postpone care
  • Less than one or two weeks after a laser procedure — we work with hydration and soothing only. Stimulation can otherwise leave darkened marks.
  • Less than two weeks after botulinum toxin or fillers — we do not use care that presses firmly on the face.
  • While taking acne medication (isotretinoin), or less than six months after stopping — we do not perform exfoliating care or waxing.
  • If you have had an allergic reaction to cosmetics, we patch-test on the inner arm first.

You cannot reach your own back. So it is harder to look after than the face, and it becomes urgent just when you have to take your clothes off.

Acne is most common on the face, but over time it can spread to the neck, back and chest. Back care divides into two things: clearing away the flakes and sebum that are hard to wash off, and releasing a back and shoulders that have become stiff.

This may suit you if
  • breakouts keep recurring on your back and shoulders
  • you want your back in order before a dress or something more revealing
  • you sit all day and your back and shoulders feel set
How it proceeds

Thorough cleansing → clearing flakes and sebum → soothing care → a moisturising mask. Care that releases knotted muscle is available as a separate programme alongside it.

What changes

The texture of the skin on the back is improved, and the set feeling eases.

※ Acne is a chronic inflammatory condition. Where care alone does not resolve it, medical treatment is needed. We tell you this honestly at the consultation.

When we postpone care
  • When inflammation has flared badly — examination comes before care.
  • Exfoliating too often actually makes skin more sensitive. We adjust the interval for you.
  • We do not treat areas with inflammation, eczema or open wounds.

By evening, the shoes you put on that morning feel tight.

Standing or sitting all day, the legs are the first thing to feel heavy. Leg care starts at the feet and calves and works up in order to the thighs, releasing legs that have grown heavy.

This may suit you if
  • your legs feel heavy and swollen by the end of the working day
  • you work standing for long periods, or sitting for long periods
  • you have had lower-body liposuction (the starting point depends on how recovery is going)
How it proceeds

Warming (foot bath or heat) → feet and calves → thighs → finishing. Circulation care, which helps fluid drain from the body, can be carried out alongside.

What changes

The heaviness and the knotted feeling in the legs ease.

※ To be honest — how much swelling or uneven-looking areas change varies greatly from person to person. Care does not reduce body fat or change body shape.

When we do not carry out care — this matters particularly for legs
  • We do not treat anyone with a clotting condition in the leg veins (deep vein thrombosis).
  • The same applies to burns, skin inflammation, eczema, wounds, fractures and advanced osteoporosis.
  • After implant surgery such as breast augmentation, circulation care begins at least two to three weeks afterwards.
  • After liposuction we use gentle releasing care so that tissue does not adhere unevenly beneath the skin; the starting point is decided by the medical team.

If you had liposuction at our clinic, we set the timing of care by following your recovery.

There are days when you could not point to any one painful place, but the whole body simply feels heavy.

Full-body care does not look at a single area. It starts at the back and continues in order through the legs, abdomen and arms. More time is spent on whichever area feels heaviest that day.

This may suit you if
  • the fatigue is general rather than in one place
  • coming several times for separate areas is difficult
  • you want to build a habit of regular care
How it proceeds

Back → legs (thighs and calves) → abdomen → arms → finishing pack. We adjust where to concentrate through consultation.

What changes

General stiffness and the knotted feeling ease, and you may feel lighter afterwards.

※ This is not a weight-loss programme. It does not aim to reduce weight or change body shape.

When we postpone care
  • Please avoid coming straight after a meal. About an hour and a half afterwards is better.
  • We do not carry it out where there is disease of the abdominal organs, a contagious illness, or a recent fracture.
  • If anything hurts during the session, say so at once. We adjust the pressure. There is no need to endure it.
  • Afterwards we recommend resting properly rather than going on to a demanding schedule.

Some people would like full-body care but cannot set aside the time.

So we divided the body into front and back, to be taken one side at a time. Today the back, next time the front — many people alternate in this way.

OptionAreas coveredUsually chosen when
Frontdécolletage · abdomen · arms · fronts of the legsthe abdomen feels bloated, or the line of the arms concerns you
Backneck and shoulders · back · lower back · hips · backs of the legsshoulders and back feel stiff, or the legs swell
This may suit you if
  • full-body care is too much in terms of time
  • one side, front or back, troubles you particularly
  • you want to keep it up steadily, alternating sides
How it proceeds

Warming → area by area in order → finishing. Front and back can each be taken alone, or as a set.

What changes

The knotted feeling on the side you chose eases. It does not structurally change the left-right or front-back balance of the body, or its shape.

※ The situations in which care is postponed are the same as for full-body care.

"Can I have a massage?" — the question we are asked most often after a procedure.

The answer is "it depends on the procedure and how long ago it was". That is why, before starting any care, we first confirm which procedure you had and when. Intensity and starting point are set by the medical team.

This may suit you if
  • you have had a procedure and need care that supports recovery
  • you need care after liposuction so that tissue does not adhere unevenly beneath the skin
  • your muscles are knotted and fatigue has built up
What techniques are used

Stroking · kneading · pressing in circles · light tapping · compression · vibration — in the terms used in medical textbooks: effleurage, petrissage, friction, tapotement, compression and vibration.

What changes — honestly

Scientific evidence on how massage produces its effects is still limited. Recent studies have reported positive results such as relief of neck and lower back pain, and when carried out appropriately it is very safe, with serious risks rarely reported. We do not claim effects beyond that range.

Possible reactions, and when we do not carry it out
  • Possible reactions — temporary pain, bruising, swelling, allergic reaction
  • When we do not carry it out — a clotting condition in the leg veins (deep vein thrombosis), burns, skin inflammation, eczema, wounds, fractures, advanced osteoporosis, disease of the abdominal organs, contagious illness
  • Starting point — no firm pressure within two weeks of botulinum toxin or fillers / two to three weeks after implant surgery / an hour and a half after eating

outro:
Booking

Care programmes run by appointment.

  • If this is your first visit, the consultation and skin assessment take a little longer, so it helps to allow plenty of time.
  • If you would like care after a procedure, simply tell us at booking which procedure you had and when, and we will check in advance which care is possible and let you know.

General notes on care programmes

  • All care follows a medical consultation; whether it proceeds and at what intensity is decided by your skin condition and the procedures you have had.
  • Results and the number of sessions needed differ from person to person. The same result is not guaranteed.
  • Temporary stinging, redness, bruising, swelling or allergic reaction may occur after care.
  • Care may be restricted where there is a clotting condition in the leg veins, skin inflammation, eczema, burns, wounds, fractures, advanced osteoporosis or an acute inflammatory condition.
  • If you are pregnant or taking any medication, please tell us when you book.
  • After a procedure, the point at which care may begin differs by procedure type. We advise you at the consultation.
